entities.name: Nitrile reduction to amine
observations: The sequence change [N][#C][C] to [N][C][C] is consistent with reduction of R-C≡N to R-CH2-NH2.
The fluorinated heteroaromatic framework is intended to remain unchanged.
Candidate reagent classes include H2 with Pd/C, Raney Ni, or PtO2; LiAlH4; and BH3 complexes.
Available ORD records do not experimentally validate this exact substrate transformation; several records retain the nitrile and report anomalous yields.

entities.name: Catalytic nitrile hydrogenation
observations: Typical candidate conditions are H2 with Pd/C, Raney Ni, or PtO2 in EtOH or MeOH at mild-to-moderate pressure.
Chemoselectivity must be checked because hydrogenation may affect heteroaromatic rings or other reducible groups.

entities.name: Borane nitrile reduction
observations: BH3·THF or BH3·SMe2 are plausible, potentially milder alternatives for reducing a nitrile to a primary amine.
Substrate compatibility with the fluorinated heteroaromatic scaffold requires experimental testing.

entities.name: Lithium aluminium hydride reduction
observations: LiAlH4 in dry ether or THF followed by aqueous workup is a standard nitrile-to-primary-amine reduction system.
It is strongly reducing and may be less suitable if other reducible heteroaromatic functions are present.
